Revenue / Campaign contribution

Media break-even ROAS

The minimum revenue-to-media multiple that covers media spend using the pre-media contribution margin. This is a campaign contribution threshold derived from margin mathematics; it does not cover fixed costs excluded from that margin.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The minimum revenue-to-media multiple that covers media spend using the pre-media contribution margin. This is a campaign contribution threshold derived from margin mathematics; it does not cover fixed costs excluded from that margin.

×

How we use it

We can set planning scenarios using the actual sales mix and variable costs, then compare achieved ROAS with the resulting threshold.

Transparent calculation1 ÷ pre-media contribution margin fraction; margin fraction = (net sales − non-media variable costs) ÷ net sales
pre media contribution margin percent40

40% is the fraction 0.40. 1 ÷ 0.40 = 2.5× ROAS to cover media spend at that margin.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Product contribution margin
  • Market and fulfillment scenario
  • Discount and return assumptions

Questions we investigate

  • Is the margin stated as a fraction in calculation?
  • Are variable costs and returns fully included?
  • Does any segment have nonpositive pre-media margin?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Recalculate margins from reconciled revenue and costs.
  • Model discount and fulfillment scenarios.
  • Use client-specific break-even assumptions in planning.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Finance and paid media leads
Review when material margin assumptions change.

Required data

  • Net sales and non-media variable costs
  • Pre-media contribution margin calculation
  • Scenario assumptions and currency policy

Read the measure with context

Zero or negative margin gives no finite positive media break-even ROAS. Zero net sales makes an observed margin undefined. Enter percentages as fractions for division. Changing prices, product mix, returns, or variable costs changes the threshold; this is not a guaranteed bidding target.
